description: Gomoku on a 15×15 board — get five stones in a row before the computer or a friend does.

faqs.a: The computer scores every empty square by the threats it creates for both sides — it takes an immediate win, blocks your open fours and threes, and otherwise builds its strongest line.
You do. Black always moves first, which is a real advantage in Gomoku — that's why the computer takes black when you choose white.
Stones can never be moved or captured in Gomoku, so draws are rare but possible if the whole 15×15 board fills up.
faqs.q: Can the game end in a draw?

howto: Pick “Vs computer” (choose your color) or “Two players”.
Click any empty intersection to place your stone.
Get five of your stones in a row — horizontal, vertical or diagonal.
The AI answers after a short think; the winning five are highlighted.
title: Gomoku
